report.headline: SA1 five‑minute RRP peaked at 4981.0 $/MWh at 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST
summary: A five‑minute Regional Reference Price (RRP) peak of 4981.0 $/MWh occurred for the interval ending 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z (2026-07-31 02:05 ACST) (evidence_id ev0436).
The analysis shows 214 five‑minute intervals at-or-above the 300.0 $/MWh threshold across the window (evidence_id ev0887; threshold evidence_id ev0888).
At the five‑minute price peak the dispatch TOTALDEMAND was 1472.82 MW and NETINTERCHANGE was -82.59 MW (net flow into SA1) (evidence_ids ev0437, ev0438).

The half‑hour containing the peak (interval ending 2026-07-30T17:00:00Z) had operational demand 1466.0 MW (evidence_id ev0913); the window maximum operational demand was 2173.0 MW (evidence_id ev0898).
The unweighted mean RRP across the window was 416.71 $/MWh (evidence_id ev0886).
AEMO published a market notice reporting a non‑credible contingency event in the SA region (quoted under published_findings; citation c1).

possible_explanations.statement: Short‑term supply tightness or limited online local generation might have allowed prices to spike; testing this would require unit‑level dispatch and availability data around the spike.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve unit‑level generation output and available capacity (SCADA/dispatch data) for the 12 hours around the spike and compare changes in output and availability immediately before and during the 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z interval.

possible_explanations.statement: A local network equipment trip (the City West transformer/circuit‑breaker event reported in AEMO's notice) could be relevant to system conditions around the event [c1]; testing would check the timing and system impacts against dispatch changes and flows.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Compare exact timestamps and system impact logs from the market notice [c1] with unit dispatch, constraint changes and the full 5‑minute NETINTERCHANGE series to see whether the network event coincided with changes in generation dispatch or interconnector flows.

possible_explanations.statement: Changes in interconnector flows or limits might have altered net imports/exports around the spike; testing would use the full 5‑minute NETINTERCHANGE series and interconnector element flows.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Fetch the full 5‑minute NETINTERCHANGE and individual interconnector element flow series across the window and examine timing of any flow reversals, ramping or constraint binding around 2026-07-30T16:35:00Z.

citations.quote: At 1140 hrs, the City West 275/66 kV transformer T_1 and the 275 kV circuit breaker 6675 tripped during restoration of City West 275/66 kV transformer T_2.
citations.supports: reports a non‑credible contingency event in the SA region on 30/07/2026

uncertainties: No unit‑level generation outputs or offer/availability data were retrieved; this limits attribution of the price spike to supply changes.

The retrieved market notice reports a transformer/circuit‑breaker trip but does not state any system‑wide impact metrics; the relationship between that event and the price spike is uncertain without time‑aligned dispatch/flow data.
missing_evidence: Unit‑level generation output and availability (SCADA/dispatch) for the 12 hours around the spike.
Full five‑minute NETINTERCHANGE and individual interconnector element flow series across the window (beyond the single value at the peak).
Participant rebids/offers, constraints and any constraint‑set changes or dispatch instructions around the event.
